problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\sqrt{{t}^{3}},$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=0\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=1\,\text{s}.$

feedback.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=-\frac{4}{(t+1)^{2}},$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=1\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=1\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{m/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int -\frac{4}{(t+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{t+1}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{4}{0+1}+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =4+C \\ C & =-\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{t+1}-\frac{7}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=1\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =\frac{4}{1+1}-\frac{7}{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{2}-\frac{7}{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{2}-\frac{7}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{3}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$
